_about: How many copies of each world-effects template the stage builds — the effect-template pool (BL-225). Each PlayEffectAt call takes the next copy, so that many overlapping calls to one effect keep their own trails/smoke at their own sites instead of collapsing onto the last one. Hand-authored engine config, NOT extracted game data: the original instances a fresh copy per CALL_ANIMATION and has no such number, so every value here is our finite approximation of 'unbounded'. Consumed by src/Session/EffectPools.cs (M3 polish-5 D10).
_premise: The 'fresh copy per CALL_ANIMATION' above is decoded, not assumed: the start gate refuses a second call on a running definition only while the concurrency bit 0x100 at +0x9c is clear, and the per-start reset sets that bit for a definition whose node tree root is a template rather than a world object, at which point the gate clones a whole new record and deep-copies the template's nodes for every further call. There is no cap in that mechanism, so every number below is this engine's finite stand-in for it. docs/org/sequences.md, 'The concurrency bit is the effect template's exemption'.
_references: The mechanism and its prohibitions: src/Mech3/TemplateStage.cs (the slot arithmetic and RootsFor) and src/Session/World/WorldEffectsFactory.cs (what each stage is built with); the module entries are docs/architecture/Mech3.md and docs/architecture/Session.md. The tuning entry: backlog.md BL-231. The root names are WorldEffectsFactory.EffectStageRoots; a name here that is not a stage root is reported, never guessed.
_sizing: slots = min(maxSlots, base + perExtraPlayer x (players - 1)). Splitscreen/multiplayer multiplies the sources: every extra aircraft is another gun and another rocket at its own site, so the per-player term is what keeps a 4-player or 16-player session from collapsing back onto one copy. maxSlots is the memory guard — each slot is one more copy of that root's subtree.
_instrument: AnimRuntime.PoolRecycles counts every call that wrapped onto a still-live slot, and the runtime names the first wrap per effect ('anim: effect pool for <name> recycled slot N of M'). A scripted run that logs none had enough pool; raise the root that logs one, not the default.

default.why: Sized against rocket concurrency: FIRE_RATE 1/s against ~2.5 s of authored trail motion means at most 3 overlapping blasts per aircraft, plus one spare. Measured: a 9-rocket burst at 1/s logged zero recycles.

gunhit.why: The gun-impact family stays SHARED on purpose (C8): gun hits are throttled to one play per 0.1 s per effect name and each instance is bounded to 0.3 s, so consecutive hits reuse one relocated copy by design at ten hits a second. Raising this without removing that throttle buys copies nothing will use. Removing the throttle is its own step, with its own emitter-count check.

dum_gunhit.why: As gunhit — the dum/ap variants' template root.

mag_gunhit.why: As gunhit — the magnesium variants' template root.

flame_ball_01.why: large_fireball, the death airburst nearly every destructible calls, and each death calls it about three times rather than once. Measured on a build with no first-use construction cost left: four simultaneous kills (--destroy=pass_plane, C1) wrap a 4-slot pool and a 6-slot one, and go quiet at 8. Bigger simultaneous kills cannot be covered inside maxSlots at all: seven (--destroy=m_build) still wrap at 16.

fire_here.why: large_30sec_fire and large_10sec_fire, which share this root and therefore share its cursor. This is an AUTHORED concurrency count, not a tune: a burning airship keeps one 30-second fire per dead part, so the number that must not collapse is the parts one hull can have burning at once. C5/M04's Dante is the largest, at 16 (14 engines, each destroy_dtz?engNN calling large_30sec_fire WITH its own supports node, plus dtznoseballgun3/4), and one broadside kill alone puts four of them up together: it calls dtzepleft_gasbag1 and dtzepright_gasbag1 8 s apart and each of those kills two engines 11 s and 22 s in, so the four fires overlap for a dozen seconds. At the old default of 4 the fifth burning part took the first one's copy back and its fire moved to the newest engine. 46 mission definitions in that one mission can start this effect. No per-player term: burning airships are world geometry.

partial_damage_obj.why: The two DAMAGE_SEQUENCE sputters (sputter_black_smoke_obj / sputter_fire_smoke_obj) live here, and damage-stage smoke is the genuinely many-at-once case: one salvo into a cluster damages several objects in the same frame, each wanting its own emitter on its own object. Measured — five simultaneous ap_h2otwr kills wrapped a 4-slot pool exactly once.

_localCallAbout: A SEPARATE, smaller pool for death-triggered CALL_ANIMATION targets that anchor on a 'library root' gamez node (docs/formats/gamez.md; AnimRuntime.ResolveLibraryRoot, 2026-08-04) — kept apart from 'roots' above because that map is validated against WorldEffectsFactory.EffectStageRoots (an unknown key there warns) and these names never are one. Sizing is the SAME three-layer answer as the effects pool: (1) pool MEMBERSHIP is the data-driven parentless-root rule, no config involved; (2) pool SIZE prefers the gamez's OWN authored duplicate count where the node list ships one — several effect templates do (sonic_ring/sonic_flare x5, mb1/mb_spinflame x5, zep_skin_fire1-4, yellow_spark_01/_02, flame_ball_01-_03, fire_here/fire_here2, muzzle_burst/muzzle_burst2 — verified same-shape single-child records, docs/formats/gamez.md), in which case N IS the original's own answer and belongs nowhere but the census; (3) 'localCallRoots' below is ONLY for a template that ships exactly one gamez record (facdsticks: single record, confirmed) yet is observed running several copies at once in the original — the original clones dynamically and the count genuinely is NOT decodable, so it is a TUNE entry same as the rest of this file. No perExtraPlayer term: these are world geometry, not per-player ordnance, and WorldSession does not carry a player count at this layer.

localCallDefault.why: A library-root template with no entry here stays single-copy (today's behaviour) unless explicitly raised — matches genx12, which is deliberately NOT pooled in this pass (kkgate is one propane tank per chapter, never overlapping itself).

_crashAbout: A THIRD pool, for the per-player crash rig's templates (BL-288) — kept apart from 'roots' (the WORLD stage's, validated against its derived root set) and 'localCallRoots' (library-root clones). The rig's bound def set (both damage-stage menus, the random_gun_impact shims, the crash family, and the airframe's own self-named destroy def) CALLs each template from several distinct sites — a panel, prop1, a wreck piece, the `destroyed` node — and one shared copy was relocated-and-restarted onto every new call site, discarding the previous site's burst mid-flight. Unlike the world pool there is no cursor: AnimRuntime.AssignCallerSlot pins each (root, call anchor, authored call event) triple to its own slot on first call. Sizes below are therefore the AUTHORED CALL-SITE counts, not TUNE guesses: per template root, the number of distinct (call anchor, call event) pairs in the transitive CALL closure of ONE rig's bound defs, maximised over the twelve rigs (a human rig plus the eleven airframes). The count is per rig kind because a rig stages one menu: a human ladder names pdpanel*, an AI ladder names pfsmoketrail/random_remote_damage, and neither names the other's. Identical in all eight chapters' cam_anim. A re-count is owed whenever the bound def set changes (EffectCatalogue.CrashRigAnimNames) or those defs do. No perExtraPlayer term: the whole rig is built once per player already. A root with no entry stays single-copy (the crash choreography templates, played once per crash).

crashDefault.why: Single copy = the pre-BL-288 behaviour, correct for every template only ever called from one anchor at a time (the crash choreography's splash/fire/steam family).

planeflakes.why: gimmeflakes debris, the busiest root in the rig. Human: one call AT each of pdp1..pdp6, four at pdp7 (offsets +2/-2/-2/-2, staggered 0.2/0.3/0.4 s) and two at pdp8 = 12. AI: short_fire_follow and short_fireball_follow each call it twice at their INPUT_NODE, over railer1/lailer1/lft_elev/rt_elev = 8.

planeflakes2.why: gimme_bigflakes — pdpanel4/6 only, one call each at pcdp4/pcdp6.

short_firetrail.why: Panel burn — pdpanel1/2/4/5/6 WITH their pdpN, plus player_damage_trail WITH prop1.

large_firetrail.why: Human: pdpanel4/6 WITH pcdp4/pcdp6, the destroy def's four pieceNseq trails WITH pieceN, and player_crash_default's own piece1/3/4 trails = 9. AI: the destroy def and ai_crash_* trail the hull at destroyed/healthy alongside the two panel calls = 4.

small_injure_fireball.why: small_fireball_follow / short_fireball_follow / short_fire_follow. AI: random_remote_damage's cascade calls twice each at railer1 and lailer1 and once each at lft_elev and rt_elev = 6. Human: pdpanel2/3/5 WITH their pdpN = 3.

flame_ball_01.why: large_fireball. Human: player_crash_dirt's four bursts and player_crash_default's two at healthy, plus p1grndhit/p2grndhit at piece1/piece2 = 8. AI: the destroy def's airburst and the crash family's, at destroyed, plus the scat_trail pair = 4 (5 on the Warhawk).

flame_ball_02.why: small_fireball — pdpanel7/8 on a human rig, short_fireball_follow at railer1/lailer1 on an AI one (the world's own flame_ball callers play on the world-effects runtime, not this rig).

yellow_spark_01.why: small_yellow_sparks — player_crash_default's five and player_crash_dirt's two at healthy, plus autogyro_loserotor's two at staticrotor1. Human rig only; no AI-bound def calls it.

yellow_spark_02.why: yellow_sparks_follow — pdpanel5 plus random_gun_impact's three WITH pdp1/2/4 shim calls.

chuteman.why: The bailed pilot. Ten airframes and player-player call it once AT destroyed; the Balmoral calls it THREE times from that one node at Event 1.0, a bomber's crew. Those three need three copies AND the per-call-site slot keying, since one slot per (root, anchor) collapses them onto one chute.

carnage_trails.why: call_crash_trails AT destroyed — one call from player_crash_default, one from _dirt and two from _water. Sticky per session, so a rig that crashes twice on different surfaces claims from both.

apassengers.why: rem_pas — the destroy def's two arms plus one per player_crash_* variant. Human rig only; no AI airframe def removes a passenger.

fuel_trail.why: player_fuelleak's three vapor calls, one each at pdp1/pdp2/pdp3.

gunhit.why: 3040slug_gunhit, called by player_fuelleak at pdp1/pdp2/pdp3. Unrelated to the WORLD stage's shared `gunhit` entry above: these are CALL_ANIMATIONs on the crash rig and take no throttle.

fire_here.why: large_10sec_fire AT destroyed — player_crash_dirt and player_crash_water, one call each.

flydirt.why: flydirt_plane — the airframe destroy def's destroyed_dirt and ai_crash_dirt's randomdestseq both land it at destroyed.

huge_splash_model.why: plane_big_splash — the airframe destroy def's destroyed_water and ai_crash_water's randomdestseq, both at destroyed.

facdsticks.why: C2's facade panels (fcpan01-39) each CALL_ANIMATION facade_parts, whose template facdsticks ships as exactly ONE gamez record — no authored duplicate count to read off. The original's own parallel debris (2026-08-04: several broken panels' four-log sets airborne at once) proves it clones the template at runtime, a count this format cannot supply. 6 is TUNE, not measured: a facade row at flight speed breaks panels roughly 0.2-0.5 s apart with each set's flight lasting 4-5 s, so a row of 8-10 panels can have 8-10 sets in the air; 6 covers most flight-through passes without recycling, at the cost of eventually wrapping (evicting the oldest still-flying set) on a longer burst.

chuteman.why: The parachutist, staged out of the aircraft archive rather than the chapter gamez (AircraftStage). This one is an AUTHORED CALL-SITE count, not a tune: CM02's ww_player calls ww_chuteman three times from wingwalk_parent, one second apart, at the same AT_NODE offset, which is the bomber crew being thrown out; each drifts for the length of its own script, so all three are in the air together. No other shipped caller asks for more than one at a time.
